title: Smoky Oyster Mushroom Carnitas
cScaleSummary: C0 because the recipe contains no cholesterol-contributing animal-derived ingredients. The oyster mushrooms, chickpeas, vegetable stock, olive oil, citrus, aromatics, spices, herbs, and corn tortillas contribute 0 mg cholesterol.
ldlActiveSummary: LDL-Active because the recipe is built around oyster mushrooms, chickpeas, vegetable stock, citrus, aromatics, herbs, and unsaturated olive oil, with texture and depth created through moisture control, browning, reduction, and skillet crisping rather than saturated fat or cholesterol-containing ingredients.
intro: Carnitas are traditionally built around slow cooking, citrus, rendered fat, and hard browning, which create a mix of tender interior pieces and crisp, chewy edges. This recipe borrows that structure rather than the meat itself. Oyster mushrooms bring their own character: delicate, savory, ragged, and crispable. Chickpeas add body and chew, while orange, lime, garlic, cumin, oregano, and smoke build the taco-stand flavor memory without turning the dish into imitation pork.

stepGroups.title: Dry-Sear the Mushrooms
items: Tear the fresh oyster mushrooms ({{quantity:fresh-oyster-mushrooms}}) into large, uneven strips. Keep the pieces irregular so thin edges can crisp while thicker pieces stay chewy.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the torn oyster mushrooms dry, without oil, and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they release moisture, shrink, and begin to brown at the edges.

Add the olive oil ({{quantity:olive-oil-first-sear}}) and fine sea salt ({{quantity:fine-sea-salt-first-sear}}). Continue cooking for 4 to 6 minutes, pressing the mushrooms into the pan occasionally, until they are browned, chewy, and lightly crisp in spots.
Transfer the browned mushrooms to a plate.

stepGroups.title: Build the Braise
items: Reduce the heat to medium. Add the olive oil ({{quantity:olive-oil-aromatics}}) to the same skillet.
Add the yellow onion ({{quantity:yellow-onion}}) and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, scraping up the browned mushroom bits, until the onion softens and begins to brown.
Add the garlic ({{quantity:garlic}}) and cook for 45 seconds, just until fragrant.

Add the ground cumin ({{quantity:ground-cumin}}), dried Mexican oregano ({{quantity:dried-mexican-oregano}}), smoked paprika ({{quantity:smoked-paprika}}), chipotle powder ({{quantity:chipotle-powder}}), ground coriander ({{quantity:ground-coriander}}), black pepper ({{quantity:black-pepper}}), and bay leaf ({{quantity:bay-leaf}}). Stir for 30 seconds to bloom the spices in the oil and onion.

Add the vegetable stock ({{quantity:vegetable-stock}}), fresh orange juice ({{quantity:fresh-orange-juice}}), fresh lime juice ({{quantity:fresh-lime-juice-braise}}), low-sodium soy sauce ({{quantity:low-sodium-soy-sauce}}), and apple cider vinegar ({{quantity:apple-cider-vinegar}}). Stir well and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, until the liquid is fragrant and slightly reduced.

stepGroups.title: Simmer with Chickpeas
items: Return the browned oyster mushrooms to the skillet.
Add the cooked chickpeas ({{quantity:cooked-chickpeas}}) and fine sea salt ({{quantity:fine-sea-salt-body}}). Stir to coat everything in the braising liquid.
Simmer uncovered for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the liquid is mostly absorbed and the chickpeas and mushrooms are glossy, sticky, and deeply seasoned.
Remove and discard the bay leaf.

stepGroups.title: Crisp the Carnitas
items: Spread the mushroom-chickpea mixture into an even layer in the skillet.
Drizzle with the olive oil ({{quantity:olive-oil-crisping}}). Increase the heat to medium-high and cook undisturbed for 3 to 4 minutes, until the bottom develops crisp browned edges.
Flip and stir in sections, then press the mixture back into the pan. Cook for another 3 to 4 minutes, until the second side has crisp bits and darker edges.

stepGroups.title: Finish and Serve
items: Turn off the heat. Add the fresh lime juice ({{quantity:fresh-lime-juice-finish}}), white onion ({{quantity:white-onion-finish}}), and fresh cilantro ({{quantity:fresh-cilantro}}). Toss once, just enough to brighten the mixture without softening all the crisp edges.
Serve with the warmed corn tortillas ({{quantity:corn-tortillas}}) and lime wedges ({{quantity:lime-wedges}}).
